target: Bu yazın en sıcak günü kırk derece olmuş.
english: The hottest day of this summer reached forty degrees.
tip: Put en before an adjective for the most: en sıcak means hottest. en sıcak günü, the hottest day.

target: Bu filmi daha önce izlemiştim ama tekrar izleyeceğim.
english: I've watched this movie before, but I'll watch it again.
tip: Verb + -mişti marks an earlier past, had done: izlemiştim means I had watched it before, prior to now.

english: You rarely wait for poetry.
tip: Siz is the polite or plural you and its verb ends in -sunuz: bekliyorsunuz means you wait, matching Siz.

english: We take the ferry across the strait.
tip: ile after a noun means by means of: feribot ile means by ferry. It can also contract to feribotla.

english: We need to go to the hospital urgently.
tip: For we need to, use verb+me plus -miz plus gerekiyor: gitmemiz gerekiyor means we need to go.

english: A ticket is needed to enter the museum.
tip: lazım means needed or necessary and follows the thing required: bilet lazım means a ticket is needed.

target: Fatma önemli bir belgeyi tercüme ediyor.
english: Fatma is translating an important document.
tip: Many verbs pair a noun with etmek (to do): tercüme etmek means to translate, so tercüme ediyor is she is translating.

english: It's raining outside, take your umbrella.
tip: The bare verb stem is the command form for sen: al means take. şemsiyeni al, take your umbrella.

english: Childhood memories always make people smile.
tip: Adding -t makes a verb causative, to make someone do it: gülümsetiyor means makes one smile, from gülümse (smile).

target: Fırıncı her sabah parkta hızlıca koşuyor.
english: The baker runs quickly in the park every morning.
tip: Add -ca/-ce to an adjective to form an adverb: hızlı (fast) becomes hızlıca, meaning quickly.

english: I succeeded in this job thanks to you.
tip: sayende is a set phrase meaning thanks to you, crediting someone for a good result: Senin sayende, thanks to you.

english: This book is very engaging, I can't put it down.
tip: Insert -ama before the ending for cannot: bırakamıyorum means I can't put it down, from bırak (leave, drop).

english: This restaurant is better than the one near the station.
tip: daha before an adjective means more, making the comparative: daha iyi means better. The thing compared takes -den.

target: Bisiklet sürmek hem sağlıklı hem eğlenceli.
english: Cycling is both healthy and fun.
tip: hem ... hem means both ... and, placed before each item: hem sağlıklı hem eğlenceli means both healthy and fun.

target: Bu dükkanda el yapımı ürünler satılıyor.
english: Handmade products are sold in this shop.
tip: Adding -ıl makes a verb passive: satmak (to sell) becomes satılıyor, are being sold, with no named seller.

target: Yıllar geçtikçe bu mahalle tanınmaz hale geldi.
english: As years passed this neighborhood became unrecognizable.
tip: Verb + -dıkça means as or the more that happens: geçtikçe means as it passes. Yıllar geçtikçe, as the years go by.

english: I wish it would stop raining.
tip: Keşke plus a -se verb voices a wish: dinse (din + se) = if only it would stop.

english: I go to school by bus.
tip: -le on a noun means by or with: otobüsle (otobüs + le) = by bus, no separate word needed.

english: How can I get to the airport?
tip: Insert -ebil for can or be able to: gidebilirim (git + ebil + irim) = I can go.

english: It is important that we arrive on time.
tip: -ma plus a possessive makes a that-clause noun: varmamız (var + ma + mız) = our arriving, that we arrive.

english: A boat passed under the bridge.
tip: Position words take genitive on the noun: köprünün altından (köprü + nün, alt + ından) = from under the bridge.

english: I walk all the way to work.
tip: -erek says by doing something: yürüyerek (yürü + yerek) = by walking, describing how you go.

english: We must prepare the report before the meeting.
tip: -malı means must or have to: hazırlamalıyız (hazırla + malı + yız) = we must prepare.

english: There are six chairs around the table.
tip: After a number the noun stays singular: altı sandalye = six chairs, sandalye not sandalyeler.

english: The places we visited on vacation were very beautiful.
tip: -dik plus a possessive makes a which-clause: gezdiğimiz yerler (gez + diğimiz) = the places that we visited.

target: Lütfen kapıyı kapatın, içerisi çok soğuk.
english: Please close the door, it's very cold inside.
tip: Add -ın for a polite or plural command: kapatın = close (formal), versus plain kapat to one friend.

target: Bahar gelince sokak kedileri daha çok görülüyor.
english: When spring comes street cats are seen more often.
tip: -ince means when or as soon as: gelince (gel + ince), so Bahar gelince = once spring comes.

target: Bisikletle işe gitmek hem sağlıklı hem ekonomik.
english: Going to work by bicycle is both healthy and economical.
tip: hem ... hem frames both ... and: hem sağlıklı hem ekonomik = both healthy and economical.

target: Meğer o çoktan gitmiş, biz fark etmemişiz.
english: It turns out he had already left, we didn't notice.
tip: Meğer plus a -miş verb marks a fact you just realized: gitmiş = turns out he had gone, not eyewitnessed.

target: Çocukluğumda her yaz köye giderdik ve yüzerdik.
english: In my childhood we used to go to the village every summer and swim.
tip: -irdi marks a past habit, used to: giderdik (git + er + di + k) = we used to go, yüzerdik = we used to swim.
